subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Psychology of Guaranteed Returns
description: One-minute skill: The Psychology of Guaranteed Returns.

hook.text: Legitimate investments fluctuate. Ponzi schemes offer suspiciously steady returns — and that's the lure.

buildup.text: Humans crave certainty. A guaranteed 10% feels safer than a volatile market averaging 10%.

discovery.text: This preference for certainty is called ambiguity aversion — and scammers exploit it expertly.

twist.text: Real markets are messy. If an investment never has a down month, something is deeply wrong.

climax.text: Madoff's steady returns were his most convincing trick. Consistency was the con.

punchline.text: Guaranteed returns guarantee one thing: fraud.

quiz.question: Why are guaranteed steady returns a red flag?
options: Real markets fluctuate — steady returns suggest fraud
